Another game that actively fights against you for trying to have fun. It doesn't respect the player at all. Its a whacky entirely chance based game where even pumping into Hit Chance and extra defences doesn't mean ♥♥♥♥ when you can suddenly be hit by a FATAL attack that just instantly kills you. I was playing one of the Tree Golem guys (dudes got massive HP gains) and completely obliterating a guy. I got him pushed to the edge of the arena, he's even getting stressed when suddenly he knifes me one time after breaking my armor and it cuts my body in half. I was full HP. Another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing about this game is buying stuff. Gold is given only if you win, losing makes you lose gold and really ♥♥♥♥♥ you over and the reason for that is because everything is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ expensive. You gotta battle a number of times before the shops get new items. Im like, oh boy, i'd really like to buy a Polearm instead of this default blunt weapon. So I open the shop, see the Polearm on sale is lvl 3 and costs 6k gold, its the only one for sale until a restock. Then im trying to save up for it and Killing my opponents for 10% extra gold on a win and when i get even close to buying that Polearm it suddenly becomes the day Restocking happens and now the weapons are higher lvl, much higher lvl than i currently am and the prices also went up a lot as well. I had to buy armor as well so that put a dent in my gold stash and kept me from buying the polearm sooner, without the armor i'd have lost those matches and lost more gold. Even checking other weapons for sale, they're all expensive for no reason at all. Not even Green Quality btw, these are basic White equipment. Basically, the game doesn't even try to make you feel strong. It's like all the good ♥♥♥♥ is always out of reach. The Hit Chance system feels unfair at times. Missing like 3-4 attacks in a row at like 66% hit chance is a REEEEE~ moment. You end up getting beat down. The games difficulty is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ absurd because of the Hit Chance system too. I tried default and it was quite unfair. Everything scales up and like i mentioned with the Gold, you just stay poor and unable to buy good ♥♥♥♥ to keep you in the game. Had a match up against a guy that seemingly healed all the time so he just out sustained me while i fruitlessly got him low and then see him full HP over and over until i died. I put it to the easiest settings after awhile and its still a little out of balance. The Fatal attack that killed me really pissed me off. The one time i felt like i was strong in this game and my character just dies from full HP when nothing is even remotely strong enough to take out 170+ HP in a single blow. It was an unearned death/loss. I lost out on around 350 gold, set back again for my weapon which btw i ended up thinking about going ANY weapon that was an upgrade and everything was again, simply too expensive or too high lvl.

I just finished Swords and Sandals III Redux and I have to say I did not expect to enjoy it this much. I already liked Swords and Sandals II Redux a lot, but Swords and Sandals III takes the formula and expands it into something much bigger. Instead of just being an arena progression game, it feels more like a full gladiator RPG adventure. I ended up beating the entire game with a Rogue subclass for the Warrior class, mainly because I wanted to use swords and focus on agility and critical damage. Apparently only around 2.3 percent of players have finished the game using that subclass, so I guess I unintentionally picked a more difficult route. Like many people, I originally played the old Flash versions when I was younger. These games were everywhere back then. You would open them on random websites and suddenly lose hours building your gladiator and fighting in the arena. Seeing Swords and Sandals III brought back properly in Redux form feels like a huge nostalgia trip, but it is also more than just nostalgia. The biggest difference compared to Swords and Sandals II is how much the game feels. This change makes much more interesting. You are not just fighting one champion after another. You are discovering new enemies, and slowly improving your character while preparing for bigger threats. It gives the game a sense that the earlier entries did not fully have. The combat itself still feels very familiar. It is turn based and heavily influenced by stats, positioning, and a good amount of RNG. Sometimes you land a critical hit and destroy your opponent in a few turns. Other times the enemy gets lucky and suddenly the fight becomes much more dangerous than expected. My Rogue Warrior build focused mostly on agility, attack power, and crit potential. When things worked in my favor the damage could be insane. Landing consecutive hits with swords felt incredibly satisfying. At the same time this kind of build is not the most forgiving. If luck goes the wrong way or you miss important attacks, the fight can quickly turn against you. That is something players should definitely expect when playing this game. Difficulty spikes are very real here. Some enemies and bosses are much stronger than the fights before them, and if your build is not properly prepared you will definitely notice. The final boss especially tested my patience. Without spoiling too much, the last battle is not something you just walk through easily. It demands strong gear, solid stats, and sometimes a bit of luck. There were multiple attempts where things went wrong because of bad RNG or one mistake in positioning. When I finally defeated the boss after several attempts it felt incredibly satisfying. Moments like that are why the Swords and Sandals games are still fun. They can be frustrating at times, but when you finally overcome a difficult fight it feels like you actually earned the victory. Another thing I noticed while playing is how clearly this game influenced later entries in the series. You can easily see why the developer reused many of these ideas and assets when creating Swords and Sandals Immortals. The structure of traveling around a world, completing quests, and fighting stronger enemies already works very well here. The art style also deserves some appreciation. It keeps the classic Swords and Sandals look but feels cleaner and more polished in the Redux version. The gladiator designs, armor pieces, and environments all maintain that slightly goofy but charming style the series has always had. Of course the game is not perfect. Just like other Swords and Sandals titles, RNG can sometimes make fights feel unfair. There will be moments where the enemy gets multiple lucky hits or where your attacks miss at the worst possible time. Some players might find that frustrating, especially during harder boss fights. There are also occasional small bugs or strange moments, which is not too surprising considering the origins of the series. Thankfully nothing I encountered was serious enough to ruin the experience. Despite these flaws, I had a great time playing through the entire game. The mix of arena combat, exploration, character progression, and ridiculous gladiator battles still works extremely well even years after the original Flash era. Beating the game with a Rogue Warrior build also made the victory feel more personal. It was not the easiest way to play, but it made every difficult fight more intense and every win more rewarding. After finishing it, I can definitely say that Swords and Sandals III Redux is one of the strongest entries in the series. It expands the formula without losing the charm that made the original games so memorable. If you grew up playing Swords and Sandals on Flash websites back in the day, this is absolutely worth playing. It captures the same feeling while offering a much larger adventure. And if you are new to the series, it is still a fun and unique RPG experience as long as you are ready for some RNG chaos along the way. Now that I finished this one, I am even more excited to continue with the rest of the Redux games. If they keep the same level of charm and challenge, I will gladly keep sending my gladiators into battle. ⚔️

I wanted to post a good review but it seems the game is extremely unbalanced. I can't really go more than two fights in a row without losing. I lowered it to the easiest difficulty from normal, and I'm still getting consistently getting defeated in a single hit by the second or even first fighter. I'm playing with a more defensive build, so it is very discouraging to be downed in a single 80 damage hit. How you're supposed to play this game on higher difficulties without losing every fight baffles me. When you look at the gladiators you can fight, the easiest one has the same level as you do with the subsequent ones having higher levels (the original game had the easiest at 2 levels under you and the 2nd easiest at 1 level under you). Facing off against the same level gladiator already feels like a challenge balanced in favor of your opponent on normal. On very easy you'll usually win vs the very first opponent, but as I said before, you can still be killed in a single hit, even with high defense. Another thing is that ranged weapon users seem to defend against like 90% of your attacks making it impossible to kill them, because they'll get hit and then heal the damage you did while avoiding the next 7 of your attacks
